newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh's conviction was written in the stars.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh's conviction was written in the stars.

text.p: For the superstitious, Timothy McVeigh's conviction for the Oklahoma City bombing on Monday was written in the stars.
It is not known if McVeigh gets the newspapers in his basement cell at the federal building in Denver, but if he read his horoscope in The Denver Post on Monday, he might have taken it as a bad omen.
The entry for Taurus, McVeigh's birth sign, read in part: "What seemed like a wonderful idea could explode in your face."
"Jacqueline Bigar's Stars", distributed by King Features Syndicate Inc., also urged Tauruses to use their "personality, wit and charm to cool down a problem."
McVeigh, a Gulf War veteran, turned 29 on April 23, a day before opening statements in the trial.
On Monday, a federal court jury found him guilty of blowing up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people in the worst attack on civilians in U.S. history.

The last line of McVeigh's horoscope might be useful advice as he confronts the penalty phase of his trial. Starting on Wednesday, the jury will debate whether he should be sentenced to death or life imprisonment.
"If possible, work on diplomacy and peace," it said.

McVeigh apparently has an interest in astrology. His sister Jennifer testified at the trial that he wrote her shortly before the bombing that "something big is going to happen in the month of the bull." Prosecutors said this was a reference to the bombing or its aftermath.
